candidates.title: Master The Art of The Kettlebell Snatch w/ This One Simple Cue
Master the Kettlebell Clean and Snatch with This Basic Drill #kettlebells
candidates.description:
The DEAD clean or snatch is a great way to clean up or learn the clean and snatch.
I use this as my primary movement with new clients regardless of their fitness level.

Here's how to do it:
Place the kettlebell between your feet, closer to the heels.
Fold at the hips keeping your chest tall and proud.
Rip the kettlebell off the floor in one swift motion allowing the bell to go over the hand.

The primary reason for this movement is to keep the kettlebell close to the body the entire time to reduce the impact on the forearm.

candidates.title: Stop making this mistake with snatches! 💪🏼 #kettlebells
candidates.description:
Wrist slamming → happens if you swing too far out and flip the bell. 

Follow these simple steps to fix it:

1️⃣ Hike the kettlebell back (like a swing)
2️⃣ Snap your hips, drive the kettlebell up
3️⃣ Elbow high → keep kettlebell close
4️⃣ Punch through at the top
5️⃣ Lock it out overhead, core tight

💡 Key takeaway is to ‘punch’ through, this allows the bell to rotate around your forearm and settle overhead smoothly.

#kettlebellworkout #kettlebellexercises #snatch #shorts

candidates.title: Improve Your Kettlebell Snatch With These Tips
candidates.description:
DO KETTLEBELL SNATCHES HURT? 

A question I get very often is, “how do you make it so the kettlebell doesn’t slam on your forearm?”

The PUNCH THROUGH! 🤜🏽

Punching through is basically extending your fist and kettlebell handle so that they both sweep under the bell.

This movement flips the kettlebell upside down so that the large part of the kettlebell makes contact with the forearm before the bell reaches its highest point. This prevents the bell from crashing down on the forearm when it’s above you.

Helpful tips:
-Don’t death grip the bell. The handle needs some wiggle room to rotate and flip the bell.
-Punch Through while the kettlebell is weightless. This is usually the point when the kettlebell loses most of its momentum. During the snatch, that’s usually right as the kettlebell is above eyebrow or forehead level.
-Practice lower punch throughs. Watch the portion of the video when I start at eye level and work my way to a full snatch.

Thanks to @Joellerblades for sharing 👑
